Any Ideas? Yes I do, some useful diagnostic information from you would be a great start.

Like what provider? That sounds very much like Yahoo, but I am done guessing as I do not know who provides the underlying mail service for Rogers.

Other critical and relevant information would be;

The exact error reported, verbatim. Whilst some error are relatively generic, they all offer useful information. Even their absence can be telling. The use of any antivirus product or a VPN. (many ISPs refuse access to their mail infrastructure, or parts of it, if you use a VPN. Regularly antivirus product make a mess of doing their jobs and no mail is received despite the connection testing Ok, this is especially so for this using third party products that either scan email, or even worse try and sort spam and scams from the mail.

You might also want to post the troubleshooting information on the help menu of Thunderbird. It has a handy copy to clipboard for pasting into other things like this forum.
